name: Pre-rendered backgrounds
summary: Rooms and streets are rendered offline in 3D software and shown as still images at fixed camera angles. The player moves as a low-poly figure, or as a cursor, over a scene with far more light and detail than the console can draw.

philosophy.core_thesis: If the camera does not move, each view can be a finished render, composed like a film frame.
design_principles: Compose each view as a still: a fixed camera with a strong diagonal or a low angle.
Render the background offline with soft shadows and many lights.
Match the real-time figure to the background with the same light direction.
Use dramatic camera angles: high, low, through a doorway.
Cut between views when the player crosses an edge.
Paint depth masks so the figure goes behind a table or a pillar.
anti_patterns: Backgrounds that the figure does not match in light
Flat eye-level views with no composition

projection_and_camera.camera: A set of fixed cameras; the view cuts as the player moves.
projection_and_camera.framing: Cinematic frames: high corners, low angles, views through doors.

geometry.primitive: An offline 3D render as a 2D image; a low-poly character on top.
geometry.budget: No limit for the background; 500–1,500 triangles for the figure.
geometry.edge_rule: Soft, anti-aliased edges in the render; hard edges on the figure.

surface.texture_rule: Detail from offline renders: wood grain, stone, stained wallpaper.
surface.texel_density: about 64–128 px for each metre at the screen size
surface.filtering: Smooth; the image is a bitmap.
surface.material_model: Offline shaders of the 1990s: Phong, reflections, soft shadows.

palette.strategy: Moody, film-like colour with a warm or a cold cast for each room.

lighting.model: Offline raytraced or radiosity light, baked into the image.
lighting.shadows: Soft cast shadows in the render; a simple blob under the figure.
lighting.atmosphere: Dust in light shafts, mist and haze baked in.
lighting.time_of_day: One fixed time for each scene, often dusk or night.

world_and_space.scale: Real scale; rooms full of furniture and objects.
world_and_space.interiors: Fully dressed rooms: libraries, halls, offices, each one view.
world_and_space.exteriors: Streets and courtyards framed like establishing shots.
world_and_space.threshold: A cut to the next camera as the figure walks through the door.

principles.rule: Place the door or the path forward at a third of the frame.
Frame the view through a door or between columns to lead the eye.
Use 3 layers: ambient, a key from a lamp or a window, and accent spots.
Put props in foreground, middle ground and background.

interface.placement: Small; often only a cursor or a menu called up on demand.
interface.type_and_icons: Serif or bitmap fonts in framed boxes.
interface.diegesis: Much is in the world: notes, books and switches in the render.

emotion.target_response: Suspense and wonder: the viewer looks at a composed, richly lit place and expects something behind the next door.

avoid_when: The brief needs a free walk-through.
The look must be clean and bright.

modifiers.how: Keep the composed angles; render with physical materials and modern global light.
Replace the render with real-time low-poly boxes and fog.
